definition: A training paradigm where models learn from unlabeled data by solving auxiliary tasks derived automatically from the data itself, such as predicting missing or masked parts.
details: Self-supervised learning enabled the current era of large pretrained models, since it allows training on vast amounts of unlabeled text, images, or audio without expensive manual annotation.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Here is the short version: A training paradigm where models learn from unlabeled data by solving auxiliary tasks derived automatically from the data itself, such as predicting missing or masked parts. The part that makes it sing: Self-supervised learning enabled the current era of large pretrained models, since it allows training on vast amounts of unlabeled text, images, or audio without expensive manual annotation. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Self-Supervised Learning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
